# 1 = favorite won
# 0 = favorite lost
# missing means no favorite at an exact 50/50 forecast

y = pd.Series(
    pd.NA,
    index=markets.index,
    dtype="Int64",
    name="favorite_won",
)

# if outcome 0 favored, use its result
favorite_is_0 = markets["favorite_index"].eq(0)
y.loc[favorite_is_0] = markets.loc[
    favorite_is_0, "outcome_0_result"
]

# if outcome 1 favored, reverse outcome 0's result
favorite_is_1 = markets["favorite_index"].eq(1)
y.loc[favorite_is_1] = 1 - markets.loc[
    favorite_is_1, "outcome_0_result"
]

# inspect the class counts, keep missing 
display(y.value_counts(dropna=False))

# make copy for decision tree model with different missing value handling 
X_train_tree = X_train_raw.copy()
X_test_tree = X_test_raw.copy()


# add cols for missing vals 
for X in [X_train_tree, X_test_tree]:

    # indicate status of large purchase as some do not include qualifying purchase 
    X["large_purchase_status"] = markets.loc[
        X.index, "large_purchase_status"
    ]

    # flag to indicate price trend is missing rather than 0 change 
    X["price_trend_missing"] = (
        X["favorite_change_pp_24h"].isna().astype(int)
    )

In [39]:
# split by col type for prep 

numeric_cols = [
    "favorite_probability",
    "observed_wallet_count",
    "large_purchase_favorite_share",
    "favorite_change_pp_24h",
    "price_trend_missing",
]

categorical_cols = ["topic", "large_purchase_status"]

# apply prep based on data type 
pre_processor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        # numeric: fill missing with median
        ("numeric", SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), numeric_cols),
        (
            # encode categorical with one-hot
            "category",
            OneHotEncoder(
                sparse_output=False,
                # if category only appears in testing, give 0 for all
                handle_unknown="ignore",
                dtype=int,
            ),
            categorical_cols,
        ),
    ],
    #remove transformer name 
    verbose_feature_names_out=False,
).set_output(transform="pandas")

# fit medians and categories to training data only, then apply transformations 
X_train_prepared = pre_processor.fit_transform(X_train_tree)

# apply same transformations with training medians and align encoded categories to test set 
X_test_prepared = pre_processor.transform(X_test_tree)

print("training shape:", X_train_prepared.shape)
print("testing shape:", X_test_prepared.shape)
display(X_train_prepared.head())

# small tree - depth = 2 
tree_depth_2 = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    criterion="gini",
    max_depth=2,
    min_samples_leaf=5,
    random_state=14,
)

# train 
tree_depth_2.fit(X_train_prepared, y_train)

plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))

# plot small tree 
plot_tree(
    tree_depth_2,
    feature_names=X_train_prepared.columns.tolist(),
    class_names=["Favorite lost", "Favorite won"],
    filled=True,
    rounded=True,
    precision=3,
    fontsize=10,
)

plt.title("Decision Tree: Maximum Depth 2")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

In [46]:
# original market probabilites from the test set
market_probabilities = X_test_raw["favorite_probability"]

# create brier score col 
brier_rows = [{
    "Model": "Original market forecast",
    "Brier score": brier_score_loss(
        y_test, market_probabilities, pos_label=1
    ),
}]

# assign brier scores for each decision tree
for depth, tree in trees.items():

    # test market probability that the favorite won 
    win_probabilities = tree.predict_proba(X_test_prepared)[:, 1]

    brier_rows.append({
        "Model": f"Decision tree: depth {depth}",
        "Brier score": brier_score_loss(
            y_test, win_probabilities, pos_label=1
        ),
    })

brier_scores = pd.DataFrame(brier_rows).set_index("Model")

display(brier_scores.style.format({"Brier score": "{:.4f}"}))

In [47]:
# individual matices for each tree depth
for depth, tree in trees.items():
    # Start a separate figure for each tree
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 4), constrained_layout=True)

    predictions = tree.predict(X_test_prepared)

    matrix = confusion_matrix(
        y_test,
        predictions,
        labels=[0, 1],
    )

    cm_display = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(
        confusion_matrix=matrix,
        display_labels=["Favorite lost", "Favorite won"],
    )

    cm_display.plot(
        ax=ax,
        cmap="Blues",
        colorbar=False,
        values_format="d",
    )

    # keep colors 
    cm_display.im_.set_clim(0, len(y_test))

    ax.set_title(f"Maximum depth {depth}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Predicted label")
    ax.set_ylabel("Actual label")

    plt.show()
In [ ]:
tree = trees[4]
loss_threshold = 0.40

# get probability that favorite lost (class 0)
loss_probabilities = tree.predict_proba(X_test_prepared)[:, 0]

# predict loss at loss_threshold or above 
threshold_predictions = np.where(
    loss_probabilities >= loss_threshold,
    0,
    1,
)

print(f"Loss threshold: {loss_threshold:.0%}")
print(f"Test accuracy: {accuracy_score(y_test, threshold_predictions):.1%}")

display(pd.DataFrame(
    confusion_matrix(y_test, threshold_predictions, labels=[0, 1]),
    index=["Actual loss", "Actual win"],
    columns=["Predicted loss", "Predicted win"],
))
